items.text: Pulumi programs can reference existing Terraform state files (as taught in the Pulumi for Terraform Users guide).
Any Terraform provider can be used in Pulumi programs.
Terraform modules can be imported and used directly in Pulumi programs.
HCL (Terraform) code can be converted to Pulumi code.
Terraform and Pulumi deployments can be orchestrated together from Pulumi.

The `@pulumi/terraform` package exposes a `terraform.state.S3Reference` class whose constructor takes `bucket` and `key` arguments and which exposes a `getOutput(name)` method for reading Terraform state outputs.
`pulumi.StackReference("<stack>")` exposes a `getOutput(name)` method for reading another stack's outputs.
The `pulumi import` command brings existing Terraform-managed cloud resources under Pulumi management.
`pulumi import` takes the form `pulumi import <type-token> <name> <id>`, and `aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc`, `aws:ec2/subnet:Subnet`, and `aws:ecs/cluster:Cluster` are valid AWS provider type tokens for it.
Pulumi provides a programmatic import API that can be called from program code to import resources (as referenced by the migration helper's `Use Pulumi import API` comment).
Pulumi policy packs (Policy as Code) can enforce infrastructure policies across both Terraform-managed and Pulumi-managed resources.

The `@pulumi/policy` package exports `PolicyPack` and `validateResourceOfType`; a `PolicyPack` takes a `policies` array whose entries have `name`, `description`, `enforcementLevel` (accepting `"mandatory"`), and `validateResource`, and the validator callback receives `(resource, args, reportViolation)`.
Pulumi's Automation API lets you embed Pulumi in applications for programmatic/dynamic infrastructure management.

The `@pulumi/pulumi/automation` module provides `LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack({ stackName, projectName, program })`, and the returned stack supports `setConfig(key, { value })` and `up({ onOutput })`, whose result exposes `outputs`.
`pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference` is available on the namespace imported from `@pulumi/pulumi/automation`.

Pulumi component resources can wrap Terraform-managed infrastructure (via Terraform state references) so that developers consuming the component do not need to know it depends on Terraform-managed resources.

A Pulumi component is created by subclassing `pulumi.ComponentResource`, calling `super(type, name, {}, opts)` with `opts?: pulumi.ComponentResourceOptions`, parenting children with `{ parent: this }`, and calling `this.registerOutputs({...})`; `pulumi.interpolate` builds Output strings.
